messages:
jess: Hi team — Acme reported a spike of 502/504s this morning on hosted inference when sending long streaming prompts. They also say they received partial responses (stream stopped mid-token) and were charged twice for the same request. Seen from their side since ~09:12 UTC. Repro steps they provided: curl + streaming websocket.

jess: Repro payload: long_prompt ~ 12k chars, model=r-instruct-3b, streaming=true, timeout=30s. Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token-omitted>. They attached a client-side log showing final chunk: \"...assistant: \'definitely\'\" then stream closed.

sarah: Thanks — can you paste the exact curl they used? Also any customer request_id or request_ids from our gateway logs?

jess: Curl they used (sanitized):
```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer XXXX\" \\ 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\ 
  -d '{"model":"r-instruct-3b","stream":true,"input":"<12k chars>"}' \\ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream
```
Customer request_id in their header: X-Req-Id: acme-2026-03-16-09:12:33

alex: I'll pull gateway logs for that request_id. My initial hunch: upstream backend node hit a hard socket timeout while streaming chunks and gateway returned 502, and our SDK retry created duplicate server-side completions which could explain double billing.

mike: Also check edge proxy keepalive settings — long streaming with intermittent inactivity can expose keepalive ttl mismatches. Which edge was this on? region=us-west-2 per customer metadata.

jess: Noted. Customer also attached a snippet from their HTTP client showing 100-continue followed by partial content and then socket EOF. They said their SDK retried with exponential backoff and got a second full response ~3s later.

sarah: OK steps I'm going to run: 1) search logs for acme request_id across gateway, runtime, billing traces; 2) check connection-close / reason codes; 3) reproduce locally with same payload and our JS/Go SDKs to see retry behaviour.

alex: Found gateway logs: timeline for acme-2026-03-16-09:12:33 ->
- 09:12:33 incoming conn accepted on edge-12-usw2
- 09:12:34 routed to runtime-pool-7 node-3
- streaming chunks start at 09:12:35
- at 09:12:37 runtime returned RST_STREAM / connection reset by peer
- gateway responded 502 to client at 09:12:37
- SDK client retried (idempotent=false) and a second request hit runtime at 09:12:40 -> completed normally
This matches the double-complete pattern.

mike: Runtime node-3 has kernel OOM/segfault alert at 09:12:36 in infra metrics, and the runtime process crashed then restarted. Crash signature points to an attention kernel on long sequence handling in quantized path. Marking for eng-runtime triage.

sarah: For immediate customer mitigation: propose a temporary policy to detect runtime node crashes and upstream-gateway map to return 503 (so SDK can retry only if idempotent) or better: return a Retry-After + do-not-double-bill? Billing team, can we flag these two request_ids for manual review?

mike: Billing can flag; I'll open ticket with billing-ops and include both request_ids (the second complete has our internal id 2026-5409001250).

alex: Repro locally using their payload + our Node SDK: I can reproduce a stream cut when running on a quantized runtime build with sequence length > 8k tokens. On non-quantized (fp16) runtime I do not see crash. So root cause likely regression in quantized inference kernel.

sarah: Nice repro. Can you paste the minimal repro steps for eng-runtime? Keep it short.

alex: Repro steps for eng-runtime:
1) checkout branch runtime/quant-kernel-hotfix
2) build runtime with q8 kernels enabled
3) run model r-instruct-3b quantized config (profile attached)
4) send streaming request with input size ~12k chars (approx 9k tokens)
Expected: runtime crashes at attention compute, producing SIGSEGV in qk_compute.c:line 214.
Observed: runtime process exits and orchestrator restarts container -> gateway sees RST_STREAM.

mike: I'll tag eng-runtime and paste logs to their channel. eng-runtime, FYI: crash signature matches previously seen qk kernel null-deref on long seq.

deploy-bot: deploy 5409001280 by sarah scheduled -> rolling back runtime-image:runtime-q8:2026-03-15 to runtime-q8:2026-03-01 on pool runtime-pool-7 (reason: crash signature on long sequences).

sarah: Rollback started. I'll keep customer updated: initial message to Acme: \"We're investigating streaming interruptions on long prompts in us-west-2. We found a runtime crash path in a quantization kernel. We're rolling back a runtime change for your region and will flag billing for duplicate completions. ETA ~30-45m.\" Can someone confirm billing flag created?

mike: Billing ticket created: BLG-4321, added both request ids and set priority P1.

jess: Customer update sent, they replied: \"thanks — please keep us posted. We rely on streaming for our UX; rollback and billing flag would be great.\" :thumbsup:

alex: Rollback finished at 09:46 UTC. runtime-pool-7 nodes back to stable image. No further crashes observed in the last 6 min.

sarah: Monitoring p95 stream errors in us-west-2; so far p95 5xx rate dropped to baseline. I'll monitor 1h and if stable close ticket.

mike: Billing confirmed duplicate-charge hold placed, awaiting manual approval for reversal.

jess: I'll follow up with customer after 1h monitoring period and confirm billing reversal once BLG-4321 is resolved.

sarah: Next steps for eng-runtime: patch qk kernel to add bounds checks and add unit test for long-sequence attention on quantized path. Also add a sentinel to runtime to return 503 with Retry-After when the runtime process is unhealthy instead of letting the gateway translate crash to 502. Tagging eng-runtime.

alex: FYI I attached the core dump and minimal reproducer in eng-runtime channel.

jess: Closing loop with customer: will send note after 60 minutes with status and billing ticket ref.

sarah: Marking thread for postmortem if billing reversal needed. For now moving to monitoring. :eyes:

mike: Leaving note in incident tracker: INC-2026-0316-usw2-quant-kernel.

jess: Thanks all — great quick turnaround.

sarah: Thanks! :thumbsup:
